name: Koppal
headline: The Devadasi system and forged age records for child marriage end girls' schooling.
summary: Koppal's reporting centres on the outlawed Devadasi system, with a 2022 survey counting about 3,600 Devadasis in the district, and on families using forged school age certificates to marry minors at mass weddings. A regional report counts over 14,000 children in agricultural work across the Hyderabad-Karnataka belt, though not by district.

reasons.detail: Poor families, often in medical debt, still dedicate adolescent daughters to temple deities, ending their schooling.

reasons.factor: Forged age records for child marriage
reasons.detail: Authorities found fabricated school age certificates used to marry minor girls at mass weddings.

Koppal girls often marry young: NFHS-5 shows 58.6 percent married before 18. Wedding season peaks around March school holidays; the Minister reported four child marriage cases in Koppal in April-May 2025.

Buses are irregular and crowded and schools far, while hostel access is limited. Girls are pulled out after menarche. High school upgrades in 2017-18 reportedly reduced dropouts in Koppal and neighbours.
Koppal is among Kalyana Karnataka districts with zero-teacher high schools; experts linked low SSLC results to missing teachers and infrastructure, and Koppal passed 53.25 percent in 2025.
Koppal recorded a 53.25 percent SSLC pass in 2025, then 93.10 percent in 2026 (rank 25 of 35), indicating volatile exam outcomes that affect Class 10 progression.
A regional report found more than a third of child labour in the Hyderabad-Karnataka belt is in agriculture; the figure is not broken down by district.
The Sphoorthi report lists seasonal migration of sugarcane workers as a disruption to children's education in Koppal villages, without giving counts.

responses.text: KHPT's Sphoorthi programme works across 51 Koppal villages, using peer girls, panchayats and Child Helpline 1098 to stop marriages and keep girls in school.
KHPT works with single-mother, tribal and poor households in 40 Koppal villages through safe spaces and Balika Panchayats to keep adolescent girls in school.
Police and the Child Welfare Committee rescued and rehabilitated child labourers during a September 2026 statewide drive.
